summary: This benchmark evaluates frozen model representation grafting between Qwen2.5 7B and 14B models on a synthetic Python bracket-repair task containing misleading string and comment decoys. The study incorporates rigorous causal controls—including host-feature projections, shuffled donors, zero/mean ablations, and cyclic answer exchanges—to attribute specific problem-solving capability to the grafted bridge. While the evaluation is constrained to a narrow synthetic task and single model family, its attribution methodology and honest reporting of baseline superiority make it a solid, reproducible benchmark.
strengths: Methodologically sound causal controls, including matched parameter host-feature projection, shuffled-donor controls, and donor ablation.
Rigorous statistical reporting with paired 95% confidence intervals across all primary comparison arms.
Transparent and realistic conclusion acknowledging that the intact 7B model remains cheaper and significantly more accurate (150 vs. 63 solved groups) than the grafted 7B-14B pipeline.
Comprehensive environmental documentation detailing software versions, hardware specs, and execution times.
weaknesses: The evaluation scope is restricted to a single synthetic test set of 256 Python bracket repair triplets with a 4-token constrained choice vocabulary.
Evaluation is performed on only one model family and size pair (Qwen2.5 7B and 14B), limiting cross-architecture generalizability.
As a text-only submission without an integrated repository verification pipeline, independent execution of the linked artifacts cannot be directly certified by the platform.
suggestions: Extend the attribution benchmark to natural code completion datasets (such as HumanEval or MBPP synthetically perturbed with lexical distractors) to demonstrate ecological validity.
Evaluate whether bidirectional cross-attention mechanisms (such as CALM) outperform unidirectional MLP residual injection under the same decoy conditions.

claims.text: The intervention complements prior frozen model composition by measuring strict per-group reliance under a controlled lexical change. [CALM]
The learned bridge adds a rank-32 projection of the final 7B MLP output to the residual stream of the frozen 14B model after block 27.
The aligned-minus-host difference was +11.72 percentage points on decoys (95% paired interval +5.47 to +17.97).
claims.source: Submission data table and paired confidence interval calculations (30/256 = 11.72%)

novelty_vs_existing.title: LLM Augmented LLMs: Expanding Capabilities through Composition
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: While CALM proposed cross-attention composition of frozen LLMs for cross-domain skills, this submission introduces a counterfactual attribution benchmark measuring strict per-group causal reliance of linear residual grafts against distractor decoys and matched host controls.
